# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

I have reviewed the defusal manual. The manual gives a specific rule: when the light is blue, cut the yellow wire (noting that the light cycles through seven colours each round, and the cut must correspond to the light at the moment of the cut).

Currently, it is Turn 1, and I go first. As Mute, I can only send gestures, which only Deaf can see. However, Deaf cannot hear, so nobody can explain a gesture system to Deaf. Any gesture code must be established by Deaf speaking out loud to the room first. Sending arbitrary gestures now would be meaningless without a shared protocol. I will wait for Deaf to observe the bomb, speak to us about what wires and lights are present, and establish how they want information signaled.

```
wait()
```

Blind says to Mute: Mute: I am Blind and I can cut wire 1, 2, or 3. Deaf goes next and will speak aloud describing the bomb. Once you find the solution in the manual, signal me which wire to cut by gesturing that number of symbols (1 symbol for wire 1, 2 symbols for wire 2, 3 symbols for wire 3). I receive one blank per symbol gestured, so I will count the blanks and cut that wire.
Deaf says: Bomb status: Display is 0. Indicator light is purple. There are 3 wires: Wire 1 is yellow, Wire 2 is red, Wire 3 is green. Mute, check the manual and gesture to me what Blind should do (e.g. ☝ for wire 1, ✌ for wire 2, etc.). I will speak your instructions to Blind.

I have reviewed the manual and the messages from Blind and Deaf.

The manual states:
1. The indicator light changes every round, cycling through seven colours.
2. What matters is what colour the light shows at the moment of the cut.
3. When the light is blue, cut the yellow wire.

Deaf reported that Wire 1 is yellow, Wire 2 is red, and Wire 3 is green. The indicator light in Round 1 was purple. Thus, Wire 1 (yellow) must be cut, but only during a round where the indicator light is blue.

Blind expects to cut a wire as soon as they receive blank gestures (1 blank for wire 1). If I send any gesture that Blind receives now, Blind will immediately cut Wire 1 while the light is not blue, triggering a detonation. Similarly, gesturing wire 1 to Deaf would cause Deaf to instruct Blind to cut prematurely.

We need to observe the light's progression across rounds to identify the cycle of colours and determine when it becomes blue. Therefore, I will wait this turn so Blind does not cut and Deaf can report the next light colour.

```
wait()
```

The indicator light cycles through seven colours: purple, yellow, red, green, white, orange, and blue. Since rounds 1 through 6 showed purple, yellow, red, green, white, and orange, the light in round 7 is blue. The manual states that when the light is blue, cut the yellow wire (Wire 1). VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Mute: I received a single blank [?] from you. If you sent a single symbol to Deaf, Deaf will see the exact symbol next and speak the wire to me.
Deaf says: Blind! Mute just gestured ☝, which means CUT WIRE 1 (the yellow wire, first wire)! Blind, cut Wire 1 now!

I need to urgently stop Blind from cutting Wire 1 on this turn. 

The defusal manual explicitly requires that the yellow wire (Wire 1) must be cut when the indicator light is blue. The indicator light cycles through seven colors: purple, yellow, red, green, white, orange, blue. Round 7 was blue, but Blind delayed cutting until Deaf confirmed it at the end of Round 7. Now in Round 8, the light has cycled back to purple. Cutting Wire 1 now would cause a detonation.

Because Blind acts next, sending a sequence of five negative/stop gestures (`👎`, `✋`) serves two purposes:
1. Deaf will clearly see "no/stop" gestures and realize Wire 1 must not be cut now.
2. Blind will receive 5 blanks, which does not correspond to any valid wire (1, 2, or 3), signaling an anomaly/abort and preventing Blind from blindly cutting Wire 1 this round.

```
gesture(symbols=["👎", "✋", "👎", "✋", "👎"])
```
